title: When The Beatles Met Elvis
note: Quotes Lennon: 'Before Elvis there was nothing'; Heartbreak Hotel inspired him to form the Quarrymen.

title: Stevie Wonder's We Can Work It Out is the greatest Beatles cover
note: Discusses Wonder's hit cover of the Beatles' We Can Work It Out.

title: You Shook Me
note: Song first recorded by Muddy Waters in 1962; Led Zeppelin recorded it on their debut.

title: Sly Stone and Prince collaboration
note: Says Prince was heavily influenced by Sly Stone; covered Sly songs 400+ times live. No mention of integrated band.

title: The 1956 song Bruce Springsteen couldn't live without
note: Elvis on Ed Sullivan was crucial and made him want to perform; guitar not mentioned.

title: Where Have All the Good Times Gone
note: Kinks song covered by David Bowie on Pin Ups (1973).

title: Song to Woody
note: Dylan's tribute to his hero Guthrie, written after visiting him in hospital.

title: Dave Murray (musician)
note: Murray took up guitar after hearing Jimi Hendrix.

title: The Basement Tapes
note: Dylan recorded the Basement Tapes with the Band, who had backed him on his 1966 tour.

title: The Architect of Discipline: Robert Fripp names the 8 albums that built his world
note: Fripp lists Sgt. Pepper among eight formative albums, as proof of what a rock record could contain.

title: In Nobel speech, Bob Dylan reminisces on 'powerful and electrifying' Minn. Buddy Holly concert
note: Dylan's Nobel lecture recalls seeing Buddy Holly in Duluth days before his death.

title: David Bowie

title: The Architect of Discipline: Robert Fripp names the 8 albums that built his world
